topic.title: Personalization and Knowledge Sharing in Federated Learning
topic.overview: Federated collaboration becomes harder when clients use different architectures, label sets, or local distributions. This topic explores what to exchange: model parameters, generated examples, prototypes, rules, or adapted components. Personalized prediction may require preserving useful local differences rather than forcing every participant into one model.
topic.whyItMatters: Incompatible representations can make naive averaging misleading, while repeated synthetic distillation can itself introduce drift. Communication efficiency therefore depends on finding a carrier of shared knowledge that clients can interpret consistently.
topic.evolution: The collection includes decentralized linear learning and Bayesian neural aggregation, followed by meta-learning-based personalization and domain generalization. Recent representatives use data-free distillation, model mixtures, and interpretable class rules to coordinate heterogeneous clients. These methods approach the same collaboration problem through different exchange formats and assumptions about available data.
openQuestions: Which shared representations transfer without confusing client-specific meanings?
How can personalization benefits be measured fairly for clients with scarce labels?
